subject: Troubles to get and display size-corrected residuals on 3D mesh.

messages.author: 5a584824866a472b
messages.subject: Troubles to get and display size-corrected residuals on 3D mesh.
parts:
Hi everyone,

I am having some issues to understand what's going on with the shapes on the min and max of the PC axes when I am using the residuals instead of the raw data. 

For the background: I landmarked caecilians skulls and I want to check for relationships between burrowing force and neurocranium shape. I performed my GPA and I got the Y.gpa$coords. I can then perform a PCA ( T1 <- gm.prcomp(Y.gpa$coords)), and try to warp my ref mesh towards the min and max of the PC1 for example. Although I don't manage to do that using the 'warpRefMesh' function, I did it with 'tps3d' and 'shade3d' functions (Grey picture). So far, so good. 

However, I would like to display the same max and min warped meshes using the residuals with the log(Csize). So I used 'procD.lm' function to get these residuals: 

plethAnova <- procD.lm(Y.gpa$coords~logCsize, iter = 999, RRPP=TRUE)
shape.resid <- arrayspecs(plethAnova$residuals,p=dim(Y.gpa$coords)[1], k=dim(Y.gpa$coords)[2])
adj.shape <- shape.resid + array(Y.gpa$coords, dim(shape.resid)) 

And I think, that here, adj.shape are my shape coordinates corrected for size as I wanted. However, if I run again a PCA on adj.shape, and I warp the ref mesh towards max-min on a PC, I have extremely weird shapes (Green picture). 

If I extract the residuals with LogCsize using another function, the Common Allometric Component function, and that I display again max and min shapes, results are totally different, but way less weird (Blue picture). 

At this point, I don't know anymore what to use to get my corrected shape variation data, and why I have so different results between the two different functions. Is there any chance I did something wrong to get the adj.shape data that could explain why I have so 'weird' shapes ? I am not saying the green one isn't correct, maybe the shape variation on this PC is located on the snout and the quadrate-squamosal complex, which would explains the weird shape. But as I have big differences between the two functions, I might have done something wrong somewhere... 

Thanks a lot! 

Best,

Aurélien

messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Troubles to get and display size-corrected residuals on 3D mesh.
parts:
Aurélien,

You need to add the mean shape to the residuals, not the original coordinates, so that your configurations resemble landmark configurations for specimens of mean size.

Below is a step to do that easily with your code.

Best,
Mike

plethNULL <- procD.lm(Y.gpa$coords~ 1, iter = 999, RRPP=TRUE)

shape.resid <- arrayspecs(plethAnova$residuals, p=dim(Y.gpa$coords)[1], k=dim(Y.gpa$coords)[2])
shape.mean <- arrayspecs(plethNULL$fitted, p=dim(Y.gpa$coords)[1], k=dim(Y.gpa$coords)[2])

adj.shape <- shape.mean + shape.resid
